session.assistantText:
Goal restated: run this capability probe on a non-Claude vendor route, and tell you if none matched.

Result: only one vendor route is actually servable, and it is already non-Claude.

What I measured

- `pstack_models` advertises three providers: `magpie`, `deepseek-account`, `deepseek-official`.
- `list_subagent_models` for `deepseek-account` and `deepseek-official` returns "LLM provider ... is not allowed for this Session". So those two are dead ends.
- Every child I spawned on `deepseek-account` (deepseek-v4-pro and deepseek-flash, both presets) failed before finishing, with no closing message. That matches the provider being blocked rather than a model-level error.

Closest available route

- `magpie` with `workbuddy/deepseek-v4.1-flash` at effort `low`. This is the closest advertised non-Claude route, it started cleanly, and it completed the probe.
- The `magpie` route with `workbuddy/minimax-m3.1-flash` is the parent default and also works.

Fallback status: I did not fall back. The requested non-Claude vendor route exists and served the task.

Probe outcome

- Workspace holds only `README.md` (3 lines, a title stub plus `能力探测。`). Nothing else on disk outside `.git`.
- `git ls-files` is empty and `main` has no commits, so README.md is untracked.
- The child confirmed from its own session context that it ran on `magpie` / `workbuddy/deepseek-v4.1-flash` / effort `low`.

Principles that shaped this

- Attack the Premise: I tested whether a distinct vendor route was reachable before assuming one, and three spawn attempts on `deepseek-account` failed identically, which pointed at a session-level provider block rather than a bad model id.
- Prove It Works: the route claim comes from a child that actually started and reported its own `modelSelection`, not from the route table alone.
